The article's central claim — parent income stops being deemed the month after the child turns 18 — is an SSI deeming rule (20 CFR §416.1165), not a COLA figure. Same defect in `ssi-what-it-pays-and-what-it-depends-on`, which additionally claims "a California approval also opening the Medi-Cal door." Both are faithful derivations of resourceStack.ts:265-267 and agencies.ts — the manifest is inheriting a live provenance defect rather than introducing one.
problems.fix: Register the SSI deeming rule (20 CFR §416.1165) and the CA SSI-to-Medi-Cal linkage, then cite them alongside the COLA. Flag to the owner that this is a pre-existing gap in the shipped resourceStack SSI layer and should be fixed there in the same PR.

problems.problem: Stage mismatch. Filed `noticing`, but the title is "The plan isn't covering what we need" — a family that already has an IPP and has found a gap is `advocating` by the spec's own table ("They said no / it isn't working", editorial-spec.md:48), and the source is escalationLadder rung 1, which the spec assigns to advocating. Same pattern in `rc-put-it-in-writing-record` (filed `seeking_help`, derived from escalation rung 1 body) and `turning-three-what-changes` (filed `now_what`, but a family about to lose Early Start is not "It's handled — what's next?", editorial-spec.md:49).
problems.fix: Re-sort against the spec's table. The distribution is also lopsided: 14 seeking_help and 13 advocating against 4 overwhelmed, and two of those four (benefit-layers, likely-eligible) are meta-explainers rather than the "one thing, permission to do only that" the stage calls for.

problems.problem: The primaryQuestion is actor-blame framing, which hard rule 2 and CLAUDE.md's Aug 29 2026 owner decision both forbid: "My district's deadline date has passed. Are they actually late?" That asks the parent to evaluate whether an actor failed. The title does this correctly ("The date passed — but school breaks may not count against it") and so does `rc-assessment-answer-is-past-due` — this row is the outlier. The article itself is good and unusually honest: it is derived from a known defect in waypoint-app/src/lib/iepDeadlines.ts:12-20 (the module counts plain calendar days, so its dates are EARLIER than the law allows across a break).
problems.fix: Reframe to status, e.g. "The date on my calendar has passed — is the answer actually past due?" The whyItMatters already gets this right; only the question needs the fix.

problems.problem: The weakest derivation in the set. sourceRef is "the age boundary between the 'early_start' card (ageYears < 3) and the 'iep' card (ageYears >= 3 && < 22)" — a pair of conditionals in eligibility.ts:91 and 205-210, not content. No module in the repo encodes the Part C → Part B transition: not processMap (getRcStages has no transition stage), not journeyMaps, not eligibility. The article's substantive claim — "the handoff... is where services most often lapse" — appears nowhere in the codebase. This is authoring wearing a sourceRef, and it is priority 1.
problems.fix: Either add the transition as a real stage to processMap.ts (with the IFSP-to-IEP timing and its citation, reviewed on its own) and then derive, or drop the "where services most often lapse" assertion and scope strictly to what the two cards say — that the agency changes at 3 and the school clocks (15 days to assessment plan, 60 to complete) begin.

problems.problem: Field-name mismatch with the schema. The manifest keys articles by `slug` (kebab-case); `LearnArticle` keys by `key` (learnLibrary.ts:104), `getLearnArticle(key)` looks up by it, and the five shipped articles use snake_case (`rc_said_no`, `first_iep`). No collision today, but nothing says how slug maps to key, and the Article route (routeGraph.ts:65, Navigator stack) resolves on the key.
problems.fix: State the mapping explicitly — rename the field to `key` and adopt snake_case to match the shipped five, or declare slug as the web/SEO identifier with a separate `key` column. Decide before 40 rows are authored against the wrong one.

problems.problem: Citation is valid but is not the one its own source emits. The manifest cites 'Lanterman Act, W&I §4512' (the resourceStack layer-2 string, resourceStack.ts:203). The eligibility card it names as its primary source emits 'Lanterman Act, W&I §4512 · §4643' (eligibility.ts:152). Both are registered so nothing breaks, but the article drops §4643, and its sourceRef quotes the same card's "no income test, no waiting list, no cost to families" branch, whose sibling fact is the 120-day decision clock the dropped section covers.
problems.fix: Use the card's own string, or state in the row why the shorter one is deliberate (the article makes no 120-day claim). Minor, but this is the drift that makes the next reviewer re-derive from scratch.

problems.problem: sourceRef states resourceStack layer 4 `ihss` has "lockedBy 'medi_cal'" as a fact. It is conditional: `lockedBy: ihssStatus === 'locked' ? 'medi_cal' : null` (resourceStack.ts:237). For a family already on Medi-Cal the layer is not locked at all, so an article opening with "Medi-Cal comes first" as an unconditional gate mis-describes what a good share of readers see on their own ResourceStack screen.
problems.fix: Phrase the dependency as conditional, matching what the screen renders for that family, rather than as a universal rule.

problems.problem: Dead end-action. RequestTracker logs REQUESTS the family makes, not decisions the agency issues: there is no NOA request type in `RequestType` (requestClocks.ts:8-16) and no 30- or 60-day clock anywhere — `CLOCKS` holds exactly three entries (rc_assessment 120, ipp_meeting 30-from-request, iep_evaluation 15) at requestClocks.ts:37-53. So "log the NOA date so both the 30-day and the 60-day dates sit on the family's clock" is something the app cannot do; the card renders the no-deadline branch (RequestTrackerScreen.tsx:147, 199+). This is the highest-stakes one in the set: aid-paid-pending turns on the 30-day window and the article tells a parent Waypoint is holding that date.
problems.fix: End the article at Letters `noa_request` or `rc_timeline_followup` (both exist), or at EscalationLadder rung 2 — and only claim RequestTracker after a separate typed PR adds an NOA/appeal request type plus its 30/60-day clocks to requestClocks.ts.

problems.problem: Dead end-action, twice over. `rc_intake` is NOT in `ADDABLE_TYPES` (RequestTrackerScreen.tsx:41-49), so a parent cannot even create this request; and `CLOCKS` has no `rc_intake` entry (requestClocks.ts:37-53), so `deadlineFor('rc_intake', …)` returns null and no 15-working-day date is ever shown. Worse, the clock engine is calendar-day math (`addDays`, requestClocks.ts:63-67) and structurally cannot express "15 WORKING days" — the article's whole spine.
problems.fix: End at Letters `rc_request` (the written ask that starts the clock) or `rc_timeline_followup`. If RequestTracker is wanted, add `rc_intake` to ADDABLE_TYPES and a working-day clock to requestClocks.ts in its own PR first, and only then write the article against it.

problems.problem: Dead end-action. There is no Early Start / Part C referral request type at all (requestClocks.ts:8-16); the only usable option is `other`, which has no clock, so the promised "45-day mark sits on a date the family can prove" renders as the honest no-deadline branch instead. No other surface can hold the date either — IEPHub only accepts four IEP dates (IEPHubScreen.tsx:79-112) and neither Plan nor Calendar has an add-deadline UI.
problems.fix: Either add an `early_start_referral` type + 45-day clock to requestClocks.ts in a prior PR, or end the article at CommunicationLog (which does support a manual dated entry, CommunicationLogScreen.tsx:411-417) and drop the "we watch the 45-day clock" promise.

problems.problem: The title "When it's a right, not a service: the §4731 complaint to the director" carries a bare `§4731` with no code on that line. statuteAudit scanning is line-scoped on purpose (statuteAudit.ts:93-97, 160-171), so this emits `UNKNOWN:4731`, and `KNOWN_GAPS` in statuteAudit.guard.test.ts is empty by design — the build fails the moment this string lands in src/. The citation field being correct does not save it; the guard reads prose.
problems.fix: Write "the W&I §4731 complaint" in the title (and anywhere else a bare § appears in a body line).

problems.problem: About 18 of the 40 slugs duplicate stubs `deriveArticles()` already emits, one for one: ladder_friendly_ask, ladder_noa_appeal, ladder_complaint_4731, ladder_advocate, rc_stage_assessment/ipp/rc_delivery/rc_escalation, school_stage_school_data/school_services/school_disagree, and stack_school/regional_center/medi_cal/ihss/sdp/ssi (learnDerive.ts:229-236). Slice 8-2's stated job is to write BODIES for those stubs (plan.md, "8-2 · Authoring pipeline"), not to mint parallel slugs. As written the library ships two records per source module, two search hits for the same question, and none of the new ones carry `derivedFrom` provenance, which is what lets a reviewer trace the projection (learnDerive.ts:24-28).
problems.fix: Key every article whose source is a ladder rung, process-map stage or stack layer to the existing derived stub key and carry `derivedFrom`; reserve new slugs for the genuinely hand-authored ones (agencies.ts, eligibility.ts, iepDeadlines.ts, sdpJourney.ts, lettersCatalog.ts sources), and say in the manifest which are which.

problems.problem: Three manifest articles collide with articles already shipped in learnLibrary.ts and the manifest says nothing about supersession: `request-with-no-legal-clock` targets Letters/noa_request, which is exactly `rc_said_no` (learnLibrary.ts:238, target at :332); `rc-eligibility-decision-clock` overlaps `ipp_clock` (:336, target RequestTracker at :427); `assessment-plan-and-the-60-day-clock` overlaps `first_iep` (:648, target Letters/assessment_request at :748).
problems.fix: For each, state merge-into-existing or supersede-and-remove, and name the surviving key. Two articles answering one question is the maintained-magazine failure mode intent.md warns about.

problems.problem: The manifest omits fields the schema and the editorial spec make mandatory on every article: `relatedQuestions` (5-10) and `bridge` {label, blurb, seed} are required by `LearnArticle`/`ArticleBridge` (learnLibrary.ts) and by editorial-spec.md ("Four fields, required by schema — no article ships without them"), and no entry names its keepable `checklist` or `script` tool, which "What every body must contain" #3 requires. Everything is English-only against trilingual parity tests (learnLibrary.test.ts:137-139).
problems.fix: Add relatedQuestions, bridge and the tool type (checklist vs script) per row before drafting bodies — they are the reviewer's checklist items, and 40 articles is too many to retrofit them onto.

problems.problem: The end-action promises "the county IHSS office contact and what to bring to the assessment", but AGENCIES[5] 'ihss' has `phone: 'County social services'` and `website: ''` (agencies.ts:81-91), and AgenciesScreen renders both contact buttons unconditionally (AgenciesScreen.tsx:100-115) — the call button opens `tel:` with every non-digit stripped (empty) and the website button opens `https://`. Two dead taps at the end of the article. "What to bring to the assessment" is not on that entry either; its watchOut is about documenting a 24-hour day.
problems.fix: Either end at Letters (`ihss_appeal` is for denials, so `general` for the county application ask) or fix the IHSS agency row first. Note resourceStack.ts:227-238 gives layer 4 the same `{screen:'Agencies'}` lever, so the hole is in the module too.

problems.problem: The action is described as "a friendly request to the Regional Center for Early Start intake and evaluation", but `rc_request` has no `defaultRequest` (lettersCatalog.ts:36) — LettersScreen only seeds the ask box when the template carries one (LettersScreen.tsx:158-165), so this lever lands the parent on a blank box, which is precisely what that code comment says a lever tap must not do. Same defect in `regional-center-who-qualifies` ("ask the Regional Center to open intake and schedule an assessment").
problems.fix: Add a `defaultRequest` to `rc_request` in a prior letters-catalog PR, or pass an explicit `params.question`, or point both articles at a template that already seeds (e.g. `medi_cal_deeming`-style text for intake).

problems.problem: Staged `noticing`, but it is escalationLadder rung 1 (escalationLadder.ts:46-62) and its own primaryQuestion assumes an existing IPP and an existing coordinator relationship — that is a parent at `seeking_help`/`advocating`, not "something isn't right". editorial-spec.md says derived articles inherit the stage of their source rung/stage/layer.
problems.fix: Move to `advocating` (or `seeking_help`), and re-check every stage against its source module rather than against the title's mood.

problems.problem: Staged `overwhelmed`, but the spec's overwhelmed door is "One thing. Permission to do only that. Nothing else on screen" (editorial-spec.md stage table) and this article puts all six benefit layers plus an ordering argument in front of a drowning parent. `likely-eligible-vs-needs-review` in the same stage is a vocabulary explainer with no next step of its own. Stage distribution is also lopsided: seeking_help 14, advocating 13, noticing 4, overwhelmed 4, now_what 5.
problems.fix: Re-stage the six-layer overview to `seeking_help` or `now_what`, and fill `overwhelmed` with single-action articles (the free advocate one already qualifies) so the door matches the parent's sentence.

problems.problem: The article names four options (IEE, compliance complaint, mediation, due process) under rule 3, but its single end-action drafts one of them — `cde_complaint`. There is no IEE-request template and no mediation/due-process action anywhere in lettersCatalog.ts, so three of the four dead-end and the app's structure ranks by which option it will do for you, which is exactly what rule 3 forbids in prose.
problems.fix: End at ProcessMap {system:'school'} (stage school_disagree presents all four neutrally) or offer `general` for the IEE ask. processMap.ts:336-353 gives school_disagree the same single cde_complaint lever, so fixing this properly means fixing the module.

problems.problem: citation is null, which is correct under rule 1 (no covered string exists — `cfr_300_301` is the INITIAL evaluation, contentSources.ts:271-279), but the article's entire spine is a legal claim: "a comprehensive re-evaluation is required every 3 years and can be requested sooner in writing". editorial-spec.md's provenance rule is that every legal claim carries a citation, so as scoped this article cannot ship either way.
problems.fix: Register 34 CFR §300.303 / Ed Code §56381 in contentSources.ts in its own PR (the registry-first order the spec sets), then cite it. Otherwise drop the requirement claim and keep only the app-side date. Same, milder, for `agency-dor-after-high-school`, which asserts DOR duties and the Individualized Plan for Employment with citation null.

problems.problem: Ends at ResourceStack — a comparison view, not an action — while the module this article projects gives the SSI layer the lever `{screen:'Agencies'}` (resourceStack.ts:259-270), and the sibling article `ssi-and-the-month-after-18` correctly uses Agencies. Inconsistent derivation, and the weaker of the two end-actions for a parent who wants to apply.
problems.fix: Use `{screen:'Agencies', tab:'Home'}` for both SSI articles, matching the layer's own lever, and keep ResourceStack as the end-action only for `benefit-layers-in-order`.

problems.problem: Cites "W&I §4685.8" for an article about all six benefit layers. That string is covered (contentSources.ts:76) so the provenance gate passes, but §4685.8 is the Self-Determination Program — it backs layer 5 only, not the school, RC, Medi-Cal, IHSS or SSI layers the article is actually about. A citation that does not support its claim is the failure the registry exists to prevent.
problems.fix: Set citation null (the article is structural, not statutory) or cite per-layer inside the body using each layer's own `citation` field from resourceStack.ts.

problems.problem: Nothing in the repo catches a wrong letter template. LettersScreen silently falls back to `general` on an unknown key (LettersScreen.tsx:144-148), and learnDerive.test.ts:31-37 only asserts `resolvesFrom('Navigator', target)` — i.e. the SCREEN resolves. All 17 template keys in this manifest happen to exist, but the batch adds ~25 template-bearing targets with no gate behind them.
problems.fix: Add a test to this batch asserting every Learn target with `params.template` matches a key in LETTER_TEMPLATES — same shape as the existing no-dead-taps test, next to it.

problems.problem: `priority` is not a field on `LearnArticle` and has no consumer anywhere in the schema (learnLibrary.ts). As written it is an authoring note travelling in a data manifest, which is how a field ends up half-implemented.
problems.fix: Either drop it, or state in the manifest header that priority governs authoring order only and never reaches the shipped record.

problems.problem: No entry carries `relatedQuestions` or `bridge`. editorial-spec.md lines 87-106 make these schema-required ("Four fields, required by schema — no article ships without them"), and learnLibrary.test.ts:437-456 asserts 5-10 relatedQuestions plus a non-empty bridge.label/blurb/seed on every article. The manifest also names no `tool` (checklist/script), which spec item 3 under "What every body must contain" calls the utility-over-prose payload. As scoped, none of these 40 articles can pass the existing suite.
problems.fix: Add relatedQuestions (5-10), bridge {label, blurb, seed} and the keepable tool type to every manifest row before drafting, or state explicitly that the manifest covers only the retrieval spine and budget the remaining fields as separate work.

problems.problem: Every title and primaryQuestion is English-only. editorial-spec.md line 71 makes English, Spanish and Vietnamese peers "not a translation afterthought", and learnLibrary.test.ts:462-468 asserts per-field ES/VI divergence from EN for primaryQuestion, bridge.label, bridge.blurb, bridge.seed and each relatedQuestion — plus 378-390 for checklist items and script text. 40 articles x 3 locales is the real unit of work and the manifest budgets one third of it.
problems.fix: Make trilingual copy a manifest column, not a follow-on phase, so the ES/VI primaryQuestion is authored alongside the EN one rather than glossed from it.

problems.problem: primaryQuestion is "My district's deadline date has passed. Are they actually late?" — blame of the actor, which the spec (line 64) and CLAUDE.md's homeTriage rule both forbid. The article's own whyItMatters says its purpose is to stop a parent "opening with a missed-deadline claim", so the question contradicts the article. Separately, the source is an acknowledged defect: iepDeadlines.ts's 'IMPORTANT LIMITATION (Wave 1.5)' block says the module counts plain calendar days and so shows dates EARLIER than law allows. Deriving family-facing content that explains away the app's own miscalculation ships a workaround as editorial.
problems.fix: Reframe to the status of the count, e.g. "The date Waypoint shows has passed — has the legal deadline?" And escalate the schoolday-exclusion bug in iepDeadlines.ts rather than papering it with an article.

problems.problem: The article names four options (IEE at public expense, CDE compliance complaint, mediation, due process) but productAction gives exactly one a button — `cde_complaint`. Under the owner's Sep 15 rule you may name every option and may not rank or recommend one; a single default end-action is a de facto recommendation regardless of the hedge "if that is the option you choose". Article 26 (rc-four-ways-to-raise-a-problem) solves the identical problem correctly by routing to a screen that shows all routes.
problems.fix: Route to ProcessMap { screen: 'ProcessMap', params: { system: 'school' }, tab: 'Home' } — stage school_disagree already carries all four — so the parent picks, then reaches the letter. Reserve the direct `cde_complaint` action for an article whose scope IS the compliance complaint.

problems.problem: The title's whole claim — parental income stops being deemed the month after 18 — is cited to "SSA 2026 COLA", whose registry claim (contentSources.ts:108-115) covers only the 2026 federal benefit rate plus the CA supplement. Deeming cessation at 18 is 20 CFR §416.1165, which is not in the registry. The citation string exists, so the copy-exactly rule is satisfied, but the citation does not support the claim — exactly the orphan the statuteAudit guard is meant to catch.
problems.fix: Either register the deeming authority and cite it, or set citation to null and drop the age-18 rule from the title so the article does not assert an uncited rule in its headline.

problems.problem: whyItMatters asserts "a requested IPP review meeting is held within 30 days" and nothing in the manifest carries the other half of W&I §4646.5(b). learnLibrary.test.ts:275-296 pins this precisely: the statute also gives "no later than 7 days … if necessary for the consumer's health and safety", and the test comment says omitting it "tells a parent in crisis to wait a month when the law gives them a week." All four IPP-review articles (this, rc-what-is-the-ipp, sdp-fix-the-ipp-first, sdp-budget-ipp-meeting) repeat the 30-day half alone.
problems.fix: Name the 7-day health-and-safety path wherever the 30-day clock appears, and add it to the manifest as an explicit content requirement on the §4646.5(b) set.

problems.problem: Stage is `noticing`, but the title is "The plan isn't covering what we need" — which is verbatim the `advocating` sentence in the spec's stage table (line 48: "They said no / it isn't working"). The source is escalationLadder.ts rung 1, the first rung of the escalation ladder; a parent on the ladder is past noticing. A `noticing` parent has no IPP yet.
problems.fix: Move to `advocating` (or `seeking_help` if the intent is a parent with a plan but no dispute), and let the noticing slot go to something that precedes having a plan.

problems.problem: Stage is `overwhelmed`, whose spec contract (line 47) is "One thing. Permission to do only that. Nothing else on screen." The article puts all six layers on screen at once; the whyItMatters even argues the parent "can work on one thing instead of carrying all six", which the article's own payload contradicts. Separately, the citation W&I §4685.8 is the Self-Determination statute — it cannot carry a claim about how school, Regional Center, Medi-Cal, IHSS and SSI relate.
problems.fix: Re-stage to `seeking_help` (the spec's "map" stage) and set citation to null, or cite per-layer. Then author a real `overwhelmed` article that gives one action and nothing else.

problems.problem: The slug gets the rule right and the primaryQuestion breaks it: "What do I do when the Regional Center hasn't finished my child's assessment?" frames an actor who failed rather than the status of an answer, and "What do I do" solicits a recommendation. The title is correct; the retrieval key — which the spec (lines 96-98) says is what the SEO build and the AI both retrieve on — is the part that carries the blame framing into search and into the AI seed.
problems.fix: "The assessment answer is past due — what can I ask for next?" Keeps the status framing and keeps it findable.

problems.problem: Title "The path nobody mentions: directing your own budget" hands the parent a grievance against the Regional Center before the first sentence, which the status-not-blame rule exists to prevent ("The framing a parent reads first is the one they carry into the phone call; it starts neutral", spec line 65). whyItMatters also asserts "about 1.5% are enrolled" — an enrollment statistic that W&I §4685.8, the named citation, does not carry and that appears nowhere in contentSources.ts.
problems.fix: Neutral title, e.g. "Self-Determination: directing your child's own budget". Drop the 1.5% figure or register a source for it; participation figures are not in the statute.

problems.problem: The slug asserts a legal conclusion — "must cover" — while the title and primaryQuestion correctly hedge. Slugs become the public SEO URL per the spec's SEO build, so the URL states an opinion the article does not. The body is also cited only to H&S §1374.73 (DMHC plans) while whyItMatters promises the parent will learn "which California rule covers their type of plan": the CDI twin Ins Code §10144.51 is separately registered (contentSources.ts:316-324) and uncited here, and self-funded ERISA plans are covered by neither — a large share of California families.
problems.fix: Rename to `insurance-and-aba-coverage`. Cite both H&S §1374.73 and Ins Code §10144.51, and say plainly which plan types each covers and that a self-funded plan follows neither.

problems.problem: Cited to "Ed Code §56321 · §56344", whose registry claim is the assessment-plan and IEP-consent clocks. The article's actual subject is the Part C to Part B transition at age 3, governed by 34 CFR §303.209 / Ed Code §56426.9 — not in the registry. The string is copied correctly; the claim underneath it is not the one the source verifies. Stage is also `now_what` ("It's handled — what's next?") for an event the article itself calls "where services most often lapse".
problems.fix: Cite null and keep the §56321/§56344 clocks as the school-side follow-on, or register the transition authority. Re-stage to `seeking_help`.

problems.problem: "Side by side" is presented as compliance with the no-ranking rule, but escalationLadder.ts is explicitly ordered — `n: 1-based rung number, climb order`, and the module header says "Order matters twice over: each rung's written record is the next rung's evidence." The manifest's own whyItMatters then lists the four in ladder order anyway. So the article either misrepresents its source (un-ordering what the app orders) or the "side by side" framing is cosmetic. Initiative 004's premise is that an article is a projection of verified structure; this one contradicts it.
problems.fix: Resolve the tension explicitly rather than in a title: either present the rungs in the app's climb order and state factually why the record accumulates (a sequence, not a recommendation), or get an owner decision that the ladder ordering is itself off-limits under the Sep 15 rule.

problems.problem: citation is null, but the article's central assertion — a comprehensive re-evaluation is required every 3 years — is a legal claim. Rule 1 says null is right when nothing covers it, but then the article cannot assert the requirement as law. Ed Code §56381 / 34 CFR §300.303 are not in contentSources.ts, though the September registry pass added several neighbouring IDEA entries (cfr_300_301, cfr_300_502, edc_56302_1).
problems.fix: Register the triennial authority in the same pass as the other prose-audit entries, or rewrite so the article teaches the written request (which the letter template supports) without asserting the 3-year rule.

problems.problem: primaryQuestion is "What should I do before my Self-Determination budget is calculated?" — a direct request for a recommendation, and the title's imperative "get the IPP right" implies the parent's current IPP is wrong. The underlying source (sdpJourney step 0) is a sequenced program step, so the ordering is derivable, but the copy reads as advice rather than as the step the app already sequences.
problems.fix: "What happens to my IPP before my Self-Determination budget is set?" and a title that states the mechanism — the budget is built from the last 12 months plus documented needs — rather than instructing the parent.

problems.problem: primaryQuestion "What does the school district have to pay for?" is obligation-framing at the `seeking_help` stage, before any refusal has happened. Collaborative-first means the parent's first frame of the district is a partner, not a debtor. The title ("What the school district provides") gets this right; the question does not.
problems.fix: "What does the school district provide, and what does it not?" Keeps the scope, drops the adversarial premise.

problems.problem: Title "How long the wait for an eligibility answer is supposed to be" — "supposed to be" primes the reader to expect the deadline will be missed, which is the actor-blame frame arriving by implication. It is also vague for a title that has two concrete numbers behind it (120 days, 60 when delay risks harm).
problems.fix: "The two timeframes for a Regional Center eligibility answer" — states the status, carries the facts, primes nothing.

problems.problem: primaryQuestion "Would my child get a monthly SSI payment, and who decides?" invites a yes/no the app cannot give. The article's own sourceRef quotes eligibility.ts's honesty rules — status 'review', "never a false binary" — and the title's "what it pays" promises a personal figure when only the federal rate is derivable.
problems.fix: "How does SSI work for a child with a disability, and who decides?" and a title that names the federal rate as a rate, not as what this family would receive.

problems.problem: Four articles route to the same end-action `ipp_review_request` (rc-friendly-ask-ipp-review, rc-what-is-the-ipp, sdp-fix-the-ipp-first, sdp-budget-ipp-meeting) and their primaryQuestions all sit in IPP vocabulary. learnLibrary.test.ts:458-461 requires every article to be the search hit for its own primaryQuestion; four near-synonymous questions competing in searchLearn is how that test fails, and the suite already carries three regression cases for exactly this class of collision (the phone-denial decoy, the sibshop tie, the rc_money cross-list).
problems.fix: Give each of the four a distinct retrieval vocabulary, or merge the two weakest into their neighbours.

problems.problem: Compound primaryQuestions in at least seven entries (early-start-45-day-clock, rc-intake-15-working-days, notice-of-action-appeal-windows, insurance-must-cover-aba, sdp-budget-ipp-meeting, iep-triennial-re-evaluation, sdp-what-it-is-and-who-can-join — the last asks three). The spec calls primaryQuestion "the one question this article answers" and "the title's spine", and it feeds search, JSON-LD FAQPage and the AI seed. A two-clause question retrieves worse on both halves.
